title: Radius: Range-based Gradient Sparsity for Large Foundation Model Pre-training
problem: Gradient communication in data-parallel LLM pre-training is a major bottleneck. Existing top-k sparsification methods fail with AdamW (causing divergence) and have poor scalability due to allgather operations whose cost grows linearly with worker count.
motivation: Dense allreduce for gradient communication accounts for ~40% of training time. Naive top-k with allgather requires O(n) bandwidth scaling, requires large HBM buffers, and is theoretically incompatible with Adam/AdamW optimizers. A scalable sparsification method compatible with AdamW is needed.
method: Radius observes that the most important gradients (top-k, the largest ones) stabilize after 15-20% of training, so it computes which ones matter once and reuses that selection for 200 steps rather than recomputing every step. Since all workers compute this same selection from combined gradient data independently, they only need to send the values of selected gradients using standard combining (allreduce) without exchanging index information, avoiding the expensive allgather step. Before computing selections, Radius applies AdamW's optimizer adjustments so that selections reflect genuine model changes. It accumulates non-selected gradients and periodically adds them back to prevent permanent information loss.
key_novelty: Leverages the fact that important gradients (top-k indices) stay mostly the same across training steps to reuse the same selection for 200 steps, replacing expensive index-sharing (allgather) with efficient combining (allreduce) while enabling compatibility with AdamW optimizers.
contributions: Discovery and validation of temporal stability of top-k gradient index distributions in LLM pre-training
Allreduce-based top-k sparsification avoiding allgather scalability bottleneck
Gradient correction ensuring correct index selection for AdamW optimizers
Error feedback mechanism preventing divergence from index reuse
19% overall pre-training time reduction on GPT-2.0B with 40% sparsity on 64 A100 GPUs
Better strong scaling efficiency than dense allreduce (42.5% vs 32.8% at 128 GPUs)
Preserved downstream task performance on GLUE, SuperGLUE, LAMBADA
limitations: Requires 15-20% warm-up training with dense allreduce before activating sparsification; very high sparsity (d=0.1) causes training instability; index resampling interval T must be tuned (default T=200); not yet extended to pipeline or tensor parallelism; tested only on pure data-parallel setting.
primary_theme: Gradient Compression / Communication Reduction for LLM Training
